feverMedicineDose.title: Children's Fever Medicine Dose Calculator
feverMedicineDose.subtitle: Work out a single syrup dose (mL) and dosing interval from your child's weight, and compare it with the matching row of the product's label table. Based on Korea MFDS guidance and approved Korean product labels.

input.title: Child and medicine
input.weightHint: Use a recent weight. The single dose is based on weight.
input.weightErr: Enter a weight between {min} and {max} kg.
input.ageHint: Used as {n} months to check the minimum age and the label table.
input.ingredientHint: Tylenol, Champ, Setopen and Coldaewon Kids Pen are acetaminophen; Brufen, Champ Ibufen and Coldaewon Kids Ibufen are ibuprofen; Maxibufen is dexibuprofen.
input.genericDesc: For products not listed, enter the strength from the leaflet
input.concHint: On a Korean label, multiply the grams per 100 mL under 'ingredients and amounts' by 10 to get mg/mL. Common syrups of this ingredient are {c} mg/mL.
input.concErr: Enter a strength between {min} and {max} mg/mL.

redFlags.title: See a doctor first in these cases
items: A baby under 3 months with a temperature of 38°C or higher
39°C or higher with a child who is clearly struggling, or any fever of 40.5°C or higher
A child who has febrile seizures, or for whom fever is risky, such as heart disease, poor nutrition or after surgery
Floppy or unusually sleepy, trouble breathing, or crying that cannot be soothed
Tiny purple spots or bruise-like patches on the skin
Stiff neck or severe headache with confusion
Fever that continues or gets worse after 3 days of fever medicine
redFlags.src: Sources: MFDS card news (2023), MSD Manual consumer version, product labels

log.title: Dose log
log.desc: Record when and how much you gave, and it works out when each ingredient can be given next. Stored only in this browser and deleted after 72 hours.
log.ready: OK now by interval and count

log.timeHint: The time is prefilled with now. A time later than now is recorded as yesterday.
log.storageError: Storage is not available in this browser, so the log is not saved.

log.overDose: More than the {mg} mg single-dose maximum
log.crossNote: Alternate fever medicines only as prescribed or directed by a doctor. When switching to the other class, wait at least {c} hours (MFDS says 2–3 hours), and never repeat the same ingredient within its interval. Ibuprofen and dexibuprofen are the same class and are not alternated.

ingredients.title: How the ingredients differ
items: Acetaminophen (the same ingredient as paracetamol): the first-choice fever reducer for children, from 4 months. 10–15 mg/kg per dose every 4–6 hours, up to 5 doses a day.
Ibuprofen: from 6 months, 5–10 mg/kg per dose every 6–8 hours, up to 4 doses a day. It also eases inflammation.
Dexibuprofen: an isomer of ibuprofen in the same class. From 6 months, 5–7 mg/kg per dose every 6–8 hours, up to 4 doses a day, sold only at pharmacies in Korea.
Common syrup strengths are acetaminophen 32 mg/mL, ibuprofen 20 mg/mL and dexibuprofen 12 mg/mL, so the same mL holds different amounts.
Too much acetaminophen can damage the liver, and ibuprofen or dexibuprofen can upset the stomach. Do not exceed the daily maximum.

alternate.title: Alternating medicines
items: Alternating does not mean giving two medicines at once. It means giving fever medicines of different classes in turn, at least 2 hours apart.
If the fever continues 2 hours after a dose, the other ingredient may be used. MFDS advises keeping a 2–3 hour gap as prescribed by a doctor.
Ibuprofen and dexibuprofen are the same class and are not alternated.
One medicine is usually enough. Alternating makes it easy to give too much, so talk to a professional.
Combination cold medicines and prescriptions may also contain a fever reducer. Check with a doctor or pharmacist before combining.

doctor.title: When to see a doctor
items: A temperature 1°C above usual or 38°C or higher usually counts as fever, and medicine can be considered depending on how the child is. Fever is a sign the body is fighting an infection, not an illness in itself.
Any fever in a baby under 3 months needs prompt medical care.
From 3 months to 3 years, see a doctor even without warning signs if the fever is 39°C or higher, there are no cold symptoms such as runny nose or sneezing, or it lasts more than 1–2 days.
From age 3, see a doctor if fever lasts more than 5 days, even if the child seems well.

Do not give fever medicine for more than 3 days without a doctor's or pharmacist's advice. The labels note that ibuprofen can strain the kidneys of a dehydrated child and that it is better avoided with chickenpox.

measure.title: Measuring syrup accurately
items: Shake suspensions well before each dose.
Measure with a cup or oral syringe marked in mL, not a kitchen spoon.
Strengths differ between products. Recalculate the mL when you switch medicines.
The single dose, interval and daily maximum are on the container, box or enclosed leaflet.
Logging the time and amount makes it easier to keep to the interval and daily maximum.

items.q: How many mL of Children's Tylenol suspension should I give?
items.a: It is 32 mg/mL acetaminophen, so 10–15 mg/kg is about 0.31–0.46 mL per kg. For 12 kg that is 3.8–5.6 mL, and the label row for 12–15.9 kg is 5 mL (160 mg). Give every 4–6 hours and no more than 5 doses (75 mg/kg) a day. Champ syrup, Setopen and Coldaewon Kids Pen have the same strength and table.

items.q: How many mL of Brufen (ibuprofen) syrup should I give?
items.a: It is 20 mg/mL ibuprofen, so 5–10 mg/kg is 0.25–0.5 mL per kg. For 12 kg that is 3–6 mL, every 6–8 hours, up to 4 doses a day. The Children's Brufen label table is split by age: 1–2 years 2.5–5 mL, 3–6 years 5–7.5 mL, 7–10 years 7.5–10 mL, 11–14 years 10–12.5 mL, 3–4 times a day, avoiding an empty stomach.

items.q: How is Maxibufen (dexibuprofen) different from Brufen?
items.a: Dexibuprofen is an isomer of ibuprofen in the same class. Maxibufen syrup is 12 mg/mL, so a dose is 0.4–0.6 mL/kg (5–7 mg/kg), up to 4 doses (28 mg/kg) a day. Because it is the same class, do not alternate it with Brufen.

items.q: How far apart should alternated fever medicines be?
items.a: MFDS advises at least 2 hours (2–3 hours in its 2025 guidance) between fever medicines of different classes. Do it as prescribed by a doctor, and never repeat the same ingredient within its interval (acetaminophen 4–6 hours, ibuprofen and dexibuprofen 6–8 hours). Ibuprofen and dexibuprofen are never alternated with each other.

items.q: From what age can I give fever medicine?
items.a: Acetaminophen from 4 months, ibuprofen and dexibuprofen from 6 months. A baby under 3 months with 38°C or higher should see a doctor first. The labels say to consult a doctor or pharmacist before giving it to a child under 2.

items.q: Should I go by age or by weight?
items.a: The acetaminophen and Maxibufen labels say a weight-based dose is more appropriate when the weight is known. This calculator works out the range from weight and shows the matching row of the label table next to it. If they differ, follow the leaflet and your doctor's or pharmacist's advice.

items.q: The fever did not come down. Can I give another dose?
items.a: Do not repeat the same medicine within its interval. If fever continues after 2 hours, the other class may be used as prescribed by a doctor. Fever medicine lowers temperature to make your child comfortable but does not treat the cause. If your child is struggling or the fever lasts more than 3 days, see a doctor.

items.q: Can I give a cold medicine together with a fever medicine?
items.a: Combination cold medicines and prescriptions may contain a fever reducer, which can double the dose of the same ingredient. Ask a doctor or pharmacist whether they contain one before combining. Paracetamol in foreign products is the same ingredient as acetaminophen.

sources.title: Sources
sources.mfds2025: Korea MFDS press note (2025-12-26), 'Don't panic when your child has a fever' — minimum ages, mg/kg, intervals, max doses a day, alternating
sources.mfds2023: Korea MFDS card news (Korea.kr, 2023-11-17), 'Using fever and pain relievers safely for children' — 2-hour alternating gap and when to see a doctor
sources.msd: MSD Manual consumer version (Korean), 'Fever in infants and children' (reviewed 2025-03) — warning signs and when to see a doctor
sources.product: MFDS approved label — {name} ({maker}): strength, dosage and precautions
sources.method: The range is MFDS mg/kg × weight. The lower mL is rounded up and the upper mL rounded down to 0.1 mL, so rounding never exceeds the single-dose maximum. Single-dose caps are ibuprofen 400 mg (label adult cold maximum) and dexibuprofen 300 mg (label table maximum); the daily cap for acetaminophen is 4,000 mg (label). The dose log uses the minimum same-class interval (acetaminophen 4 hours, ibuprofen and dexibuprofen 6 hours), 2 hours across classes, and the 24-hour count and total.
sources.asOf: Checked {date}. Labels can change, so also check your product's leaflet.
